text.content: Twelve years later, the Larchmont is still standing, a black box gutted from the inside: four stories of blackened brick, windows with no glass, a construction fence with a demolition notice nobody ever acted on. The rain comes in through the roof and falls down the stairwell to the basement, where you can hear water running. On the fence, someone has left seven plastic flowers tied on with wire.

A pack of three Sabbat Kindred who didn't leave for the Gehenna War used the Larchmont's basement as a farm: they kept seven tenants locked in the old cistern and fed on them for weeks.

One of Montgomery's contacts tipped him off. The Sheriff sent David. David arrived after the pack, warned, had already set the building on fire to erase the trail. The seven tenants were already dead. He destroyed two of the three. The third escaped through the storm drain into the Sound (@UUID[JournalEntry.AnZpyM4onyACPwiC.JournalEntryPage.18vJtyOOVZe1Uk41]{GAN-09 · The Larchmont Survivor}).

Montgomery ordered the cistern sealed without removing the bodies: seven bloodless corpses were a Masquerade breach. Danny Ruiz (@UUID[JournalEntry.5xUDUgkyHXGD8IPY]{Danny Ruiz}) is still down there.

The photo of David with his back to the fire, in the File, is from that night.

Scene: @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.9fTKL8Oeq36BCfU9]{A2-E05 · The Ashes of the Larchmont} (optional). If the coterie opens the cistern, Thermometer +2 (). If David is there or finds out, he breaks: the Storyteller plays it. What they tell Helen is up to the players. If @UUID[JournalEntry.fVXK7vOoqn0ZL0uf]{Helen} ever learns it, the Touchstone relationship changes forever.
